scope: Read-only source review of the owner-qualified native-pair identity path and contract changes. No live host/provider/DB/browser calls, no tests, and no code edits.
findings: The contract now distinguishes provider-authenticated identity from NATIVE_OWNER_CONFIGURED_PAIR provenance and says explicitly that the latter is an owner-configured association, not a provider-issued crosswalk. This resolves the earlier contract conflict without claiming Ozon attested the Seller/Performance relationship.

Performance credentials are first sent to the existing real token endpoint. Only a bounded, strict successful token response proceeds to binding resolution. Any token/auth failure stays AUTH_DENIED/IDENTITY_NOT_VERIFIED and cannot consult binding to override it.

Binding resolution is fail-closed on every request: root-owned non-writable file-chain checks, no-follow bounded JSON reads, read-only systemd credential check, exact environment/product/provider/kind/tenant/store scope, one matching row, active account/execution, exact native store/credential binding, current native credential material, both qualification records and revision-bearing native store source. It uses domain-separated keyed HMAC and constant-time comparison for the exact Performance pair; raw API key/secret is not copied into the projection or returned.

Canonical identity is derived only from the seller_client_id inside the currently working native Seller credential paired with its seller_api_key in the same native credential object; the projection binds both Seller and Performance pairs. It does not derive a Seller cabinet from Performance client ID, token/JWT, name or a report endpoint. Platform finish still checks exact equality against the already verified store identity, revision/security state and tenant-local duplicate constraint.

The platform adapter accepts provenance only for PERFORMANCE and only for the exact enum. finish stores a distinct internal check code and audit event, while the customer projection reports CONNECTED with an explicit binding_provenance field. No secret, HMAC or raw identity is exposed. A different Seller identity is still rejected as ACCOUNT_MISMATCH; unsuccessful replacements preserve active credentials.

The runtime package builder now includes the canonical native_store_binding.py and marks the feature as opt-in/otherwise unlinked. The duplicated qualification checker is synchronized. The tests add deterministic scope, secret/client mutation, source drift, revocation, ambiguity, auth-failure and unlisted-pair cases, plus integration persistence/audit/account-mismatch coverage; CI remains a separate gate.
trust_boundary: The HMAC key and scope projection are root-controlled together. Their integrity ultimately relies on the root-owned, non-writable configuration boundary and operator authority, not on HMAC against a malicious root administrator. This provenance must remain labeled as owner-configured rather than provider-authenticated.
remaining_gates: Exact full CI and package manifest/source review must pass before installation.
The live checker module integration must be reviewed against the exact active runtime preimage while preserving the foreign additive catalog method and existing HTTP primitive.

Owner-qualified pairing permits identity binding only; advertising operation capabilities/scopes still depend on current native qualification and do not independently imply every campaign/report operation is safe.
Full AL-S05 completion still requires separately authorized real provider checks and verified customer-visible behavior; this source review does not perform them.
